facts.heading: Tomas is nervous about therapy
facts.content: Tomas is quite nervous about attending therapy.
facts.evidence: I am quite nervous, if I am to be honest.

facts.heading: Wife prompted therapy attendance
facts.content: Tomas's wife suggested he seek therapy because things could not continue as they were.
facts.evidence: My wife. She says it can't go on like this.

facts.heading: Compulsive checking behavior
facts.content: Tomas checks if he locked the door and turned off the stove thirty times a night.
facts.evidence: Thirty times a night I check if I locked the door and turned off the stove,

facts.heading: Time taken to leave apartment
facts.content: It takes Tomas an hour to leave his apartment.
facts.evidence: it takes me an hour to leave the apartment.

facts.heading: Checking routine details
facts.content: Tomas's routine involves locking the door, going to the elevator, returning to pull the handle, checking the stove knobs separately, and checking the door again.
facts.evidence: I lock the door, I go to the elevator, I come back and pull the handle. Then I check the stove, every knob separately. Then the door again.

facts.heading: Relief followed by anxiety
facts.content: After checking, Tomas feels relieved temporarily, but then an image comes to his head that he didn't do it properly, causing him to check again.
facts.evidence: I feel relieved for a while. And then an image comes into my head that I didn't do it properly, and I have to do it again.

facts.heading: Fire image appears daily
facts.content: Tomas sees a clear image of the apartment on fire daily.
facts.evidence: The apartment on fire. I see it clearly, like a film.

facts.heading: Anxiety peaks in evenings/mornings
facts.content: The anxiety is worst in the evening when they go out or go to sleep, and also in the morning.
facts.evidence: It's the worst in the evening when we go out or go to sleep. In the morning too.

facts.heading: Onset linked to neighbor's fire
facts.content: Tomas's issues started two years ago after the neighbors' house caught fire and they evacuated.
facts.evidence: It started two years ago when the neighbors' house caught fire and we had to evacuate.

facts.heading: Experience of neighbor's fire
facts.content: Tomas experienced the neighbor's house fire at night when the alarm woke him up, and he watched the windows burn from outside in the winter.
facts.evidence: The alarm woke me up. There was smoke in the hallway and people were screaming.

facts.heading: Feeling of causing fire
facts.content: Since the fire, Tomas has felt that he can cause it, and if he doesn't control something, it will happen and he will be to blame.
facts.evidence: Since then I have the feeling that I can cause it. That if I don't control something, it will happen and I will be to blame.

facts.heading: Inability to stop checking
facts.content: Tomas knows the logic but cannot stop the checking behavior.
facts.evidence: I know it doesn't make sense. I know the logic. But I can't turn it off.

facts.heading: Anxiety response to resisting
facts.content: When he tries to let go, anxiety grows until he feels like he is going crazy, leading him to prefer checking.
facts.evidence: And then anxiety grows in me, until I feel like I'm going crazy. I'd rather do it.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms of anxiety
facts.content: Tomas experiences heart symptoms, sweating, shaking hands, and feeling sick in his stomach due to anxiety.
facts.evidence: Heart, sweat. My hands shake and I feel sick in my stomach.

facts.heading: Wife is aware of the issue
facts.content: Tomas's wife, Barbora, knows about the issue.
facts.evidence: Barbora. My wife.

facts.heading: Wife's perception of issue
facts.content: Barbora has moved from seeing it as a habit to seeing that it is more serious.
facts.evidence: At first she took it as a habit, now she sees that it's more.

facts.heading: Wife's patience is exhausting
facts.content: Tomas observes that his wife's patience is exhausting her.
facts.evidence: I see that it is exhausting her.

facts.heading: Late arrival at cinema
facts.content: Tomas arrived at the cinema forty minutes late yesterday.
facts.evidence: Yesterday we arrived at the cinema forty minutes later.

facts.heading: Wife waited for checks
facts.content: Barbora waited outside for Tomas to return and check the stove for the third time yesterday.
facts.evidence: She waited outside for me to return and check the stove for the third time.

facts.heading: Tomas's feelings of shame
facts.content: Tomas felt shame and felt like a child who couldn't leave the house.
facts.evidence: Shame. I felt like a child who can't leave the house.

facts.heading: Tomas's job as electrician
facts.content: Tomas works as an electrician in Olomouc. He does wiring in apartments and houses.
facts.evidence: I work as an electrician in Olomouc. I do wiring in apartments and sometimes in houses.

facts.heading: Fear of making wiring mistake
facts.content: Tomas is afraid he will make a mistake connecting a wire incorrectly and something will burn.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid that because of my head I will make a mistake once.

facts.heading: Checking behavior after jobs
facts.content: Tomas checks after every job, sometimes going back the next day just to look.
facts.evidence: after every job I go back and check. Sometimes I go back the next day, just to look.

facts.heading: Colleagues' perception of Tomas
facts.content: Tomas's colleagues think he is a pedant.
facts.evidence: They think I'm a pedant.

facts.heading: Boss's view of Tomas's care
facts.content: Tomas's boss considers him the most careful in the company.
facts.evidence: The boss tells me I'm the most careful in the company

facts.heading: Time cost of checking
facts.content: In the last few months, checking makes Tomas work an hour more per day.
facts.evidence: In the last few months, it makes me work an hour more per day.

facts.heading: Handing over jobs to colleague
facts.content: Tomas has handed over a few jobs to a colleague because he couldn't manage them.
facts.evidence: I have already handed over a few jobs to a colleague because I couldn't manage it.

facts.heading: Fear of losing job
facts.content: Tomas is afraid he will lose his job, especially now.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid I'll lose my job. Especially now.

facts.heading: Barbora's pregnancy status
facts.content: Barbora is four months pregnant.
facts.evidence: Barbora is four months pregnant.

facts.heading: Waiting for pregnancy
facts.content: Tomas and Barbora waited for the pregnancy for three years.
facts.evidence: We waited for it for three years.

facts.heading: Intrusive thoughts about harming
facts.content: Tomas has thoughts that he will harm Barbora and the baby.
facts.evidence: That I will harm her and the baby.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur during daily tasks
facts.content: Tomas fears the thoughts might happen while cutting bread or standing by the stairs.
facts.evidence: maybe when I'm cutting bread or standing by the stairs.

facts.heading: Not telling Barbora about thoughts
facts.content: Tomas has never told Barbora about these thoughts.
facts.evidence: I've never told anyone about it, not even Barbora.

facts.heading: Coping with intrusive thoughts
facts.content: When the thought appears, Tomas leaves the room or goes back to check something.
facts.evidence: I leave the room. Or I go back and check something to make it stop.

facts.heading: Checking helps calm intrusive thoughts
facts.content: Tomas believes checking helps calm the intrusive thoughts.
facts.evidence: Actually, yes. It never occurred to me that they were related.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Tomas sleeps terribly and wakes up twice at night to check the stove.
facts.evidence: I sleep terribly. I wake up twice at night and check the stove, even if there is nothing on it.

facts.heading: Activities that help Tomas
facts.content: Going for walks with Barbora or fixing things at home helps Tomas.
facts.evidence: Going for walks with Barbora helps me. Or when I fix something at home, it keeps me busy.

facts.heading: Frequency of walks and repairs
facts.content: Tomas walks with Barbora twice a week and repairs when something needs fixing.
facts.evidence: Walks twice a week, repairs when there is something.

facts.heading: Goals for future
facts.content: Tomas wants to leave the apartment in five minutes and wants to look forward to a child without certain thoughts.
facts.evidence: To leave the apartment in five minutes. And to look forward to a child without those thoughts.

facts.heading: Fear of exposure therapy
facts.content: Tomas heard about therapy where a person is gradually exposed to what they are afraid of.
facts.evidence: I heard about therapy where a person is gradually exposed to what they are afraid of.

facts.heading: Fear of being forced
facts.content: Tomas was afraid someone would force him to leave the door open and go.
facts.evidence: I thought someone would force me to leave the door open and go.

facts.heading: Acceptance of small steps
facts.content: Tomas finds the idea of checking the door once to be big for him.
facts.evidence: But even that is big for me.

facts.heading: Feelings for Barbora
facts.content: Tomas told the therapist that he loves Barbora.
facts.evidence: That I love her.

facts.heading: Need for treatment to keep Barbora
facts.content: Tomas stated he needs to get treated so he doesn't lose Barbora.
facts.evidence: And that I need to get treated so I don't lose her.

facts.heading: Fear of Barbora's feelings
facts.content: Tomas is afraid Barbora wouldn't want to be with him.
facts.evidence: Right now I'm afraid she wouldn't want to be with me.

facts.heading: Barbora's expected reaction
facts.content: Tomas believes Barbora would hug him.
facts.evidence: She would probably hug me.

facts.heading: Tomas's willingness to share
facts.content: Tomas stated he could handle telling Barbora about being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I could handle that.

facts.heading: Plan for door check
facts.content: Tomas agreed to try checking the door once when leaving the apartment.
facts.evidence: Once. I'll try it.

facts.heading: Plan to rate discomfort
facts.content: Tomas agreed to write down a number from one to ten regarding his discomfort.
facts.evidence: and I'll write down a number from one to ten.
